topic: the 897 Cadaver Synod trial of Pope Formosus's corpse
title: The Pope Who Put His Predecessor's Corpse on Trial
description: AI-narrated commentary on the 897 Cadaver Synod, when Pope Stephen VI dug up his dead predecessor Pope Formosus and put the corpse on trial in Rome.

hook_candidates.text: In 897, a decaying corpse sat on a throne, on trial for its own crimes.
Why did a 9th-century pope dig up his dead predecessor and put him on trial?
Most people think a church trial always needs a defendant who's still alive.
Nine months after Pope Formosus died, Stephen VI had his corpse dug back up.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks their annoying boss is the pettiest person alive, because they want to prove medieval Rome did pettier.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume a trial always needs a defendant who is still alive, not a decaying corpse.
closing_comment: Formosus's corpse was thrown in the Tiber after the trial, but a monk supposedly fished it back out.

sources.note: Confirms Formosus's corpse was tried, found guilty, stripped, and thrown into the Tiber.
Confirms Stephen VI was overthrown, imprisoned, and strangled later in 897.
